title: A Multi-Source Urban Water Quality Dataset for Seasonal Analysis

notes.text: This study presents a multi-source urban water quality dataset collected from 18 monitoring sites across a large metropolitan area. The paper focuses on seasonal variation, water chemistry indicators, and spatial differences between upstream, midstream, and downstream locations.
Li Ming, Chen Yu, Wang Tao, and Emily Zhang. Corresponding author: emily.zhang@example.edu
Published in Journal of Environmental Data Science, 2025, Volume 12, Issue 3, pages 88-112. DOI: 10.1234/jeds.2025.0318.

The dataset includes CSV tables, calibration logs, sensor metadata, sampling schedules, and a README describing column definitions. File formats: CSV, TXT, XLSX, and JSON. Download page: https://data.example.org/water-quality

Samples were collected monthly between March 2022 and February 2024. Measurements include pH, dissolved oxygen, conductivity, turbidity, nitrate, phosphate, ammonia nitrogen, and temperature. Quality control followed a two-stage validation process with manual review and automated outlier detection.
urban water quality, seasonal analysis, monitoring network, dataset, environmental sensing, spatiotemporal variation
Supported by the National Natural Science Foundation and the City Environmental Monitoring Program. Grant numbers: NSFC-2024-1007, CEMP-2023-44.

Users should cite both the article and the dataset. The dataset license is CC BY 4.0. Missing values are marked as NA. The dataset is intended for reproducibility studies, baseline model training, and environmental trend analysis.
